title: Pharmacy ownership restrictions (Western Australia)
summary: In Western Australia, with limited exceptions, only registered pharmacists may own a community pharmacy business, under the Pharmacy Act 2010 (WA), and there is a limit on how many pharmacies one pharmacist may own. The limit in Western Australia is four.

instruments.title: Pharmacy Act 2010 (WA)
instruments.provisions: who may own, or hold an interest in, a pharmacy business

direction_rationale: Ownership rules keep supermarkets, chains and other investors out of community pharmacy and cap how large a pharmacist's business can grow. The Harper Review found the ownership and location rules are not needed to ensure quality of care and recommended removing them.

industries.name: Pharmaceutical, Cosmetic and Toiletry Goods Retailing

verified.notes: An existing setting: no commencement date is recorded. The Act and its limit of four pharmacy businesses per pharmacist were found on the WA legislation site through search results. The ACT and the Northern Territory also restrict ownership, but their laws could not be verified; Queensland's regime is the 2025 reform record.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 28 October 2026 (phase 4, second tranche, of the productivity framework pivot) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: Only pharmacists may own pharmacies, and each may own only a few. It keeps other investors and business models out of community pharmacy; the Harper Review recommended removing the restriction.

marks.reason: Reserves ownership of pharmacies to pharmacists and caps how many each may own: an exclusive right to enter.

assessment.confidence_note: The restriction is explicit; its effect on prices and access has not been measured in Australia.
